articleTitle: Construction Method of Knowledge Graph of Manufacturing Resources in Cloud Manufacturing Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: In order to find processing task resources conveniently and provide knowledge support for the formation of cloud manufacturing resource pool, this paper proposes a method to construct knowledge graph of manufacturing resources under cloud manufacturing environment. Firstly, according to the basic process of knowledge graph construction, A scheme of knowledge extraction and knowledge fusion of manufacturing resources under cloud manufacturing environment is designed. Then, by analyzing the types, attributes, constraints and other characteristics of resources in the cloud manufacturing environment, an ontology model of manufacturing resources in the cloud manufacturing environment is constructed based on class-level network and class iteration. Finally, combined with a specific case, an interactive visualization analysis method of knowledge graph is designed to verify the application of resource discovery in cloud manufacturing environment.

articleTitle: The Measurement of the Elastic Modulus and Kinetic Friction Coefficient of Long Nanowires by the Micro-force Probe in the SEM Combined with Finite Element Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: As an important nanomaterial, nanowires have important applications in micro-nano manufacturing, biomedicine, nano power generation and other fields, and are one of the current research hotspots. The traditional deformation-based nanowire dynamic friction measurement method only calculates the kinetic friction coefficient based on the deformation of the nanowire. However, due to the lack of force feedback, a certain pre-load force needs to be applied, which will also introduce errors and cause inaccurate measurement results. At the same time, it is easy to cause damage to the tungsten needles and nanowires, which is not suitable for nanowire samples with large aspect ratios. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes a method for measuring the elastic modulus and kinetic friction coefficient of Silicon (Si) nanowires (NWs) based on the combination of measurement of micro-force probes in the scanning electron microscope (SEM) and the simulation of the deflection of NWs. First, the corresponding relationship between the deformation of the nanowire and the force was obtained. Secondly, the influence of different elastic modulus and kinetic friction ratios on the deformation of nanowires were calculated by the simulation. Finally, the experimental data and simulation results are matched, and the elastic modulus and kinetic friction proportional coefficient with the smallest error is selected. The measurement method avoids the influence of the pre-load force on the measurement result, and at the same time avoids damage such as fracture of the nanowire and the probe due to excessive force. The effectiveness of this method is proven by comparing the measurement results in this article with the values in the relevant literature.

articleTitle: A New Omni-Directional EMAT Using Contra-flexure Coils for Plate Inspection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: Ultrasonic guided wave testing method, especially Lamb wave, is perfectly effective in nondestructive testing of complex structures like plate. Lamb wave excited by Lorentz force has the advantage of large detection range. However, the traditional transducer is difficult to identify the ultrasonic signal accurately because of its bidirectional propagation from one coil. To address this problem, a novel omnidirectional electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) with two contra-flexure coils (CFCs) is designed to achieve omnidirectional one-way propagation. At the same time, the ultrasonic signals are enhanced, which improve the signal to noise ratio. Through modeling and simulation, it is proved that the new transducer is more effective in omnidirectional energy transmission than the traditional one.

articleTitle: Catalytic Graphitization of Amorphous Coal at Low Temperature and its Application in Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: In this work, using coal as raw materials (RC), which is one of the cheapest natural carbon sources and most abundant, and converted to coal-based carbons (CBC) by catalytic activation followed with Low temperature graphitization, the XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and TEM/FFT results confirmed the structural transformation from amorphous to the crystalline structure. The electrochemical performance was investigated using electrochemical methods, (CBC) anode delivered stable charge/discharge capacities compared with the (RC) anode, and stable cycle life of 243 mAh g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> can be acquired after 100 cycles with a coulombic efficiency over 98 % at 0.2C current density; this attributed to the contributions of the porous and crystalline structure, considering the low cost, easy preparation, and good performance, the coal-based carbons can be a good candidate instead of graphite as the anode materials of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs).

articleTitle: Task Decomposition and Restructuring Method for Collaborative Design of Crowdsourcing Platform
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: In the crowdsourcing design environment, the crowdsourcing design tasks published by the demand subject need to be decomposed into subtasks with appropriate granularity, so that the crowdsourcing platform can match the design tasks and design resource subjects accurately. In order to solve the problem of low efficiency of bilateral matching between subtasks and design resource subjects in complex design tasks in crowdsourcing plat-form, this paper proposes a design task decomposition and restructuring method based on design structure matrix and genetic algorithm. Firstly, based on the decomposition requirement of the crowd-sourced design task, de-composing the requirement task of the demand subject into several subtasks, and carrying out a design structure matrix modeling among the subtasks. On this basis, re-structuring each subtask based on genetic algorithm. Finally, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed method by a case that decomposing and restructuring of a design task of automobile appearance crowdsourcing.

articleTitle: Liquid Metal Based Stretchable Sensor for Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: In recent years, liquid metal materials have gradually attracted widespread attention from scholars at home and abroad due to their unique fluidity and high conductivity. Especially in the field of flexible electronics, there are endless researches on preparing liquid metal into various stretchable electronic circuits, sensors, and intelligent systems. Besides, researchers have also developed a variety of liquid metal functional materials and various liquid metal based flexible circuit preparation methods. In this research, we printed liquid metal on a stretchable substrate to prepare a stretchable sensor, which exhibits good electrical stability and can detect the movement of human body or robot joints. We believe that this kind of liquid metal stretch sensor can have broad application prospects in the fields of smart sensing, wearable electronics, and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Continuous Production of Conductive Fiber by Depressing Plateau-Rayleigh Instability for Wearable Smart Textile
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: The highly conducting polymer fiber with robust electrical conductivity and strain durability is the fundamental component of electronic textiles (E-textiles). Through alternately coating of 1D nanosize electric conductive materials and carbon black/polyurethane composite on nylon-6 fiber, we realized the continuous production of conducting fiber. The single wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) and Ag nanowires (AgNWs) were used as the conducting elements. By using designed soft confined nozzles, the Plateau-Rayleigh instability (PRI) of coated fluid layer were depressed effectively. The 50μm thick nylon-6 fiber coated with 2 μm ~ 4 μm thick shell exhibits conductivity of 30 Ω/cm ~ 80 Ω/cm and maintains 80% conductivity after 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> repeat folding test. The fiber with lamella shell shows great strain durability Within 50% strain and fully recovered conductivity within 30% repeated strain. The electrothermal effect of the yarns was measured and the low frequency electrocardiogram (ECG) signal and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) signal transmission using yarns was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Silica-Derived From Rice Husk Ash Nanofluid for the Machining of Aluminum Alloy: Effect on Cutting Force, Tool Wear and Surface Roughness
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: This work presents the analysis of low-cost SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-derived from rice husk ash (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-RHA) nanofluid on the machining of Aluminum alloy. The turning operation was conducted at a cutting speed of 250m/min, feed rate of 0.3mm/rev, depth of cut of 0.6mm, machining time of 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350sec, and 1.5wt%SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-RHA nanofluid. The SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-RHA nanofluid has a higher significant effect in lowering the tool wear, cutting force, and good surface finish. The total reduction in tool wear gained with the nanofluid was 47.57%. The results establish that the low-cost rice husk waste can be used in the production of efficient nanofluid for the machining (turning operation) of aluminum alloy.

articleTitle: A Prism Based Structure is Developed through Design Thinking Method to Improve the Performance of Automatic Optical Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: The traditional method of appearance defect detection is to rely on the examiner's personnel senses identification, but people's vision is lack of standard, and it is easy to cause false detection or missed detection due to fatigue or inattention. Therefore, the use of automatic optical inspection equipment, is the use of machine vision instead of human eyes to carry out quality inspection, in addition to improving inspection quality and efficiency, but also reduce the cost of human resources, but the cost of automatic optical inspection (AOI) equipment is not low, for the traditional furniture wood processing, economic factors are the biggest obstacle to implement. Another reason is that there are great differences among length, width and height. Generally, the width is much larger than the height. Therefore, the sheet can be put on the conveyer along the length direction. However, for the narrow side, turning and erecting need fixture. There are many ways to solve problems in traditional industrial engineering, such as DMAIC and 8D methodology. Most of them belong to the vertical mode thinking method. This mechanism design uses the lateral mode thinking method, adopts the five stages of design thinking, and creates the auxiliary mechanism design with the principle of prism reflection, which is simple and solves the procedure operation of avoiding turning over and vertical detection. The design can simultaneously detect the front side, left side and right sides of the wood board, and verify the design performance of high efficiency and low cost.

articleTitle: Study on the Aging Performance of Propellant under Humid and Hot Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: In order to further explore the aging mechanism and physical nature of solid propellants under the combined action of moisture and heat. This paper uses HTPB and NEPE as the research objects to carry out propellant storage aging tests under damp and heat conditions to monitor the changes in the mechanical properties, Shore hardness, moisture absorption rate, and impact sensitivity of the propellants in real time during the test, and further explore the two aspects in terms of the influence mechanism of the factors, the similarities and differences of the performance of the two propellants are compared and analyzed. The study found that during the damp heat aging process, the mechanical properties of the propellant declined severely, the maximum tensile strength, fracture strength, etc. dropped sharply, and the Shore hardness and the quality of the propellant changed to varying degrees. The impact sensitivity of NEPE is much lower than that of HTPB, and because NEPE contains a large amount of high-energy solid additives, the sensitivity values of the two are inconsistent during.

articleTitle: Study of Ice Accretion Using an Open Loop Portable Icing Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: Icing tunnels have great importance for icing study in many engineering applications like aviation, electrical power transmission, wind energy and climate research, where it can be used to create replicas of different types of icing on structures in controlled environment at different operating and geometric conditions. This paper presents a simple design of an open loop icing tunnel designed by students of UiT. Preliminary experiments have been carried out to simulate the ice accretion on rotating cylinder of different diameters for different icing conditions. A rotating multi-cylinder assembly is used for the experiments and results show that different types of icing can be simulated in this icing tunnel. A novel feature of this icing tunnel is its portability that makes it suitable for the field experimentation.

articleTitle: High Electrical Conductivity AgCuTe0.9Se0.1 for Supercapacitor Electrode Material
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: AgCuTe species have been proved to be an interesting materials in the field of thermoelectric. However, our recent research find that it is also particularly attractive for the supercapacitor system. Supercapacitors, which are distinguished of their high power density, long cycle life and fast charging/discharging rates, are expected to be widely used in energy storage devices. Herein, we first synthesize the metal chalcogenide-based AgCuTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf> with high electrical conductivity (733 S cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>@300K) for supercapacitor electrode. Specifically, it exhibits high specific capacitance of 2124 F g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at a current density of 1 A g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 987 F g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at a current density of 10 A g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Moreover, it exhibits super-long cycle life (83.0% retention rates after 8,000 cycles at high current density of 10 A g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>). We speculate that this phenomenon may be attributed to the highly conductive of AgCuTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf> itself, which simplifies the diffusion of electrolyte ions to access active materials and facilitates the rapid electron transport. Further, we will try to explore the in-depth analysis to understand whether there is a certain mechanism for applying thermoelectric materials to supercapacitors. Totally, our work find a new AgCuTe electrode material for supercapacitor, which is of paramount importance for advanced energy storage devices.

articleTitle: The Characterization of Nanocomposites from Poly(lactic acid) with Nanocarbon Black as the Reinforcement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: Carbon black and Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) were melting blended to prepare conductive nanocomposites, and melamine was used as the compatibilizer. The effects of nanocarbon black (CB) content on mechanical properties, hydrophobicity, electrical crystalline and morphology of PLA/CB nanocomposites were investigated. The results presented that the tensile properties and hydrophobicity of PLA/CB nanocomposites improved simultaneously by adding appropriate amount of CB, but the mechanical properties of PLA/CB nanocomposites decreased by adding too much CB. The conductivity test results showed that there was no significant change after CB content exceeded 12%. This is due to the CB aggregation. XRD results showed that the main crystallization peak of CB increased with the increase of its content, and the addition of CB did not affect the crystal form of PLA.

articleTitle: The Era of the Creative Minds-The Role of Nanomaterials to Achieve Sustainable and Innovation Architecture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: Building and construction is the fastest growing market sector that has a major impact on increasing environmental pollution. Therefore, it has become essential to review in-depth the technology of material science to reduce their negative impact on the environment and their application on the innovative building structure. Recently, great attention has been given to the application of Nano materials that play a crucial role in a sustainable and ecological lifestyle. Furthermost, the potential to enhance more eco-friendly and sustainable possibilities without compromising the efficiency, structure, durability, cost-effectiveness, and productivity are of key importance. However, understanding the use of this new technology is essential to convey the advantages of such technology to achieve a sustainable design to attract the willingness and openness from architects, engineers, developers, manufacturers, and building owners. The aim of this research is therefore to provide new insight into nanomaterial and their use to comprehend the necessity of the designer/architect to be intellectually aware of the fresh innovations and trends to keep up with modern technique and practical understanding of ''smart'' materials.

articleTitle: An Imperfection Sensitivity Analysis on Buckling of Laminated Composite Cylindrical Shells
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: Buckling is an instability problem which occurs under compressive forces on slender structures, and it happens suddenly without warning. Therefore, calculating correct critical buckling load is important for thin walled structures. Including imperfection in the analysis is very important since buckling loads with imperfection are far lower than the buckling loads obtained by assuming that they are perfect. Ignoring the initial imperfections may cause unexpected failures. It is possible to classify the imperfections as geometric, material or loading. Among them, the geometric imperfection has the highest effect on the critical buckling load. In this study, the influence of geometric imperfection on the buckling of axially loaded composite cylindrical structures is investigated. A parametric study is conducted to determine how the imperfection sensitivity can vary with the length to diameter ratio, stacking sequence, and the shape of the imperfection. For this purpose, Finite Element Analyses (FEA) are implemented by using a commercial FEM code, ABAQUS. In numerical simulations, the imperfection for all parameters is changed from 10 percentage to 100 percentage of the shell thickness

articleTitle: Best Conditions for an Ionic Implantation of Particles into Carbon Nanotubes with Usage the Channeling Effect
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: The problems of the critical parameters for ion channeling in carbon nanotubes and criteria of the radiation defects formation at such channeling are considered. The best conditions for an ion implantation into nanotubes with channeling effect combination are proposed.

articleTitle: Changes in Wave Spectrum under Impact of the Breakwater Construction over the West Sea in Ca Mau Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: It has been years since many measurements were applied to reduce wave energy and protect infrastructure and the coast from erosion through alluvial processes. The common way to test the effectiveness of the protection measurement is based on wave degradation coefficient analysis by considering the wave height (Hs) values in the front and backward of the breakwater constructions. This method is widely used because of its advantage in analyzing the effectiveness of construction directly. However, this method does not provide the wave degradation processes statistically. This study used observation data measured at several constructions at the West Sea in Ca Mau province in Vietnam and applied Fourier spectrum analysis method to deeply investigate the structure and propagation process of wave spectrum and its variation in amplitude and shape under the impact of centrifugal concrete embankment in the tidal area.

articleTitle: Reinforcement of Polymer Bio-Composite with Melon Shell Particles for Engineering Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Nanoscience and Technology (ICNST)
abstract: There have been global research efforts dedicated to developing cost-effective composite materials with high sustainability properties. A lot of materials have been tested in this drive, especially materials and combinations of materials thought to enhance engineering properties. An investigation into the development of bio-composites with improved properties using epoxy/melon shell particles reinforcement is presented. The study employs experimental research design techniques. In execution, the solution casting technology was the choice for producing the experimental samples. The matrix material used was Epoxy LY 556 resin while HY951 acted as the hardener. A matrix-hardener mixing ratio of 10:1 by weight was used. During the tests, the melon shell particles (MSP) maintained a 5 percent weight stepwise variation through 30% weight in the epoxy matrix. The results shows that incremental addition of the MSP particles leads to significant increase in all the mechanical and electrical properties of the composite. Also, the result show a point of inflection in the tensile strength after the 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> weight percent MSP addition, while other quantities maintained a proportional increment with percentage weight MSP increase. The resulting composites can therefore be recommended for enhancing selected electro-mechanical properties in outdoor and indoor engineering materials consideration.
